items.title: Procurement Act 2023, section 19: Award of public contracts following a competitive tendering procedure
items.quote: must disregard any tender from a supplier that does not satisfy the conditions of participation
items.why: The binding rule that gives a Carbon Reduction Plan its force. A contract goes to the most advantageous tender, judged against the published award criteria, but a tender from a supplier that fails a condition of participation is not assessed at all. So a sustainability requirement set as a condition is a gate, not a score.

items.title: Procurement Act 2023, section 12: Covered procurement: objectives
items.locator: s.12(1)(a) to (d) and (4); commencement note I2
items.quote: have regard to the fact that small and medium-sized enterprises may face particular barriers to participation
items.why: The objectives every public buyer must have regard to: value for money, maximising public benefit, transparency and integrity, and the barriers smaller suppliers face. 'Public benefit' is the statutory hook for social and environmental considerations; the section does not mention sustainability by name. In force 24 February 2025.

items.title: PPN 006: Taking account of Carbon Reduction Plans in the procurement of major government contracts
items.quote: should include, as a condition of participation, a requirement for bidding suppliers to provide a CRP
items.why: The policy itself. Central government departments, executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies should require a plan confirming a commitment to net zero by 2050 from bidders for contracts above the stated annual value, where relevant and proportionate. Formerly PPN 06/21. It binds central government buyers; other public bodies and private buyers are not covered.

items.title: PPN 006: Frequently asked questions
items.locator: Questions on how plans are assessed and on emissions data
items.quote: Supplier CRPs should not be ‘scored’ or compared against each other
items.why: Corrects the idea that a better carbon record wins more marks. Assessment is a check that the plan meets the requirements; the emissions data in it 'is not to be used as a basis for assessment in the procurement process', and a rise in emissions does not fail the plan. Policy statements or case studies cannot be accepted in place of the plan.

items.title: PPN 002: Taking account of social value in the award of central government contracts
items.quote: In-scope organisations must apply a minimum 10% weighting (or an equivalent measurement) of the total score, for social value.
items.why: Where sustainability can earn marks. Central government must weight social value in scoring and write suppliers' commitments into the contract. The accompanying Social Value Model (read alongside) lists environmental benefit, including working towards net zero, as one outcome among several that a buyer may select, so the marks are for what the bidder commits to do on that contract, not for its general credentials. Applies to procurements begun on or after 1 October 2025.

items.title: National Procurement Policy Statement
items.locator: Section on the government's missions, 'Make Britain a clean energy superpower', PDF page 4; later section on small and medium-sized enterprises
items.quote: taking account of environmental risks and ensuring suppliers are committed to high environmental standards
items.why: The statement all contracting authorities must have regard to under section 13 of the Procurement Act 2023, so its reach is wider than central government. Sets net zero and environmental standards among the priorities for public buying, alongside spend with small businesses. In effect from 24 February 2025 'until it is withdrawn, amended or replaced'; laid by the previous government and still shown as current on gov.uk today.

items.title: Review of the Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLL) Market: letter to Heads of ESG/Sustainable Finance
items.locator: Summary findings, p.2; 'Conflicts of interest and weak incentives to issue SLLs', p.3
items.quote: Small savings on margins may be outweighed by costs and negotiation time with lenders or legal advisors.
items.why: Source of the quotation and the figure. The regulator's findings from talking to lenders and borrowers: margin step-ups for missed targets of around 2.5 basis points, capped at about 5, for investment-grade borrowers (25 to 30 for lower-rated loans); the market slow to develop for mid-sized and smaller firms; a view among banks that the relationship may matter more than sustainability credentials. Limits: based on engagement in March and April 2023, not a data study; the FCA says it does not directly regulate this market.

items.title: The Issuance and Design of Sustainability-linked Loans (Working Paper 23-027)
items.publisher: Loumioti and Serafeim; Harvard Business School
items.quote: sustainability-linked lending has been available mostly to borrowers with low ESG risk profiles
items.why: Research on who gets sustainability-linked loans. Finds they have gone mostly to borrowers already rated low-risk, and describes the market as a way of signalling credentials at an early stage of contract design. Limits: a working paper, not peer reviewed in this version; syndicated loans to large companies worldwide, so it says little about small UK firms.

items.title: The greening of lending: mortgage pricing of energy transition risk (Staff Working Paper No. 1,016)
items.quote: We find no evidence of lenders charging higher rates on riskier mortgages against energy-inefficient properties.
items.why: The only UK lending-price evidence found, and it cuts against the idea that lenders reliably price what they can see: across 1.8 million UK mortgages originated before 2018, lenders did not charge more on energy-inefficient homes. Limits: mortgages, not business loans; the period before lenders were pressed to act; a staff paper that does not state Bank policy.

items.title: Making environmental claims on goods and services (Green Claims Code guidance)
items.locator: Sections 'Claims must be truthful and accurate', 'Claims must be substantiated' and 'Business-to-business claims'
items.quote: They should hold robust, credible, relevant and up to date evidence that supports them.
items.why: The limit on commercial use of sustainability credentials. Claims must be true, clear, and backed by evidence the business holds. Written chiefly for claims made to consumers; it says it also applies, to a more limited extent, to businesses marketing to other businesses. Published in 2021, before the consumer law it rests on was replaced in 2025; whether the guidance has been reissued was not checked.
